articles.title: Managerial turnover means we need new ways to predict Premier League fixtures
articles.summary: With 110 matches to feature two coaches appointed this year, tactical history may be more insightful than teams’ head-to-head records. New managers are facing an almost one-in-two chance of being fired before the end of the season, a finding from Guardian analysis that shows 22 of the past 50…
body: The betting markets reflect this reality. Six of the eight Premier League managers deemed most likely by bookmakers to be next to leave their post were appointed in 2026. Football management is a very precarious employment position. It looks inevitable that some of the 11 men who have only been in their role since earlier this year will fall before the end of the 2026-27 season – even if none of them are the first to move on.

Vítor Pereira, Graham Potter and Thomas Frank became managers of Wolves, West Ham and Tottenham respectively in 2025, started last season in those roles and yet were removed by mid-February of this year at the latest. Across the preceding decade, 25 men who started a season as a new manager, appointed in that year, did not see out the season in question.

All of which raises an interesting question. Where once we might have looked at the head-to-head record between two clubs ahead of a clash, should we now focus on the managers instead? What they bring tactically and how quickly they can implement their ideas is increasingly relevant at the top level of English football.

articles.title: Ordonez's move to Palace in doubt after medical
articles.summary: Club Brugge defender Joel Ordonez's move to Crystal Palace runs into complications after his medical, with the Eagles set to make a final decision about whether to proceed with the deal.
body: BBC Sport reported this week that Palace had hijacked Aston Villa 's move for the Ecuador centre-back and agreed an initial loan for Ordonez that included an option to buy at the end of the season.
The 22-year-old is recovering from a broken metatarsal, which Palace were aware of when negotiating the deal, but the injury is understood to be worse than the Eagles originally believed.
Palace have accelerated their efforts to sign a new centre-back after Chadi Riad was taken off on a stretcher against Everton on Saturday.
They completed a deal to sign Axel Disasi on loan from Chelsea on Wednesday but want to add another central defender to the squad.

articles.title: I'd hate to finish career like this - O'Sullivan
articles.summary: Ronnie O'Sullivan says he does not "want to throw in the towel just yet" after losing 6-3 to Chang Bingyu in the semi-finals of the Wuhan Open.
body: The seven-time world champion fought back against China Open winner Mark Selby in the quarter-finals on Thursday to seal a 5-3 victory, but he has spoken candidly at this week's ranking event about his struggles.
O'Sullivan has taken steps to prioritise his mental health in recent years, withdrawing from tournaments and discussing his battles with depression and anxiety.
"The disease came back big time today," said the 50-year-old Englishman. "If I'm honest I don't think I will ever get over it."

O'Sullivan, who has not won a ranking event for more than two years, added: "I will see out the next 18 months and see how we go. I don't want to throw the towel in just yet. I've committed to playing until then.

articles.title: NI's Howe relishing 'surreal' experience at Celtic
articles.summary: From Maguiresbridge to Celtic, Casey Howe has already packed plenty into a career that has taken her across the UK and Ireland - but her latest chapter may be the most exciting yet.
body: A Northern Ireland debut at 17, a treble-winning season with Glentoran, a move to Nottingham Forest and promotion with Wolves have all helped shape the County Fermanagh native, who is now testing herself at one of the biggest clubs in Scottish women's football.

The 23-year-old got off the mark for Celtic on just her second appearance for the club last Sunday, with a beautiful left-footed curler that finally broke the deadlock in the 82nd minute of an eventual 3-0 win over Montrose in the Scottish Women's Premier League (SWPL).
"Being just a young girl from Maguiresbridge, it is pretty surreal to do this," Howe told BBC Sport NI.

The road to the state-of-the-art training centre at Barrowfield in the East End of Glasgow was one paved with long journeys, family sacrifice and a belief that one day she could reach the highest level.

articles.summary: Alan Forrest hopes his prominent role in last weekend's derby victory can help ignite his Dundee career. The 29-year-old winger, who joined from Hearts this summer, marked his start by assisting Owen Bevan's goal as Dundee emerged with a 2-0 win at Tannadice.

"For me, it's just about getting minutes in and adding what I can to the team. We're all chipping in for the same goals and if I can add to that, that's what I'm looking to do.

articles.title: Panthers host Texans Friday for final preseason game; starters sit out
articles.summary: The Carolina Panthers will host the Houston Texans at 7 p.m. Friday at Bank of America Stadium for their final preseason game of the year. Head coach Dave Canales confirmed earlier this week that the team’s starters will not play in the matchup.
body: The contest follows a rough joint practice between the Panthers and Texans. Carolina quarterback Bryce Young and the offensive unit struggled during the workout, with Young getting sacked at least six times.
Despite the difficult practice, Young said the offensive group remains unified and focused on growth.

“Our whole unit, whoever is out there, there’s no one out there, I would want to be with so it sucks to have a day where you don’t feel like you produced very well, but it’s a great learning opportunity that’s what these training camp practices are for,” Young said.
Channel 9 will air live coverage featuring player interviews and postgame analysis immediately following Friday night’s game.

articles.title: Ex-NBA All-Star Goes OFF After Jonathan Kuminga Lands $12.4M Wolves Contract
articles.summary: Jonathan Kuminga spent months waiting for his next NBA contract. At 23 years old, the former No. 7 pick still had the age, athleticism and flashes of production that made him one of the league's most interesting young forwards.
body: His next deal, however, did not look like the payday that usually follows that profile. The Minnesota Timberwolves gave Kuminga a two-year $12.4 million contract with a player option for the second year. That number only makes sense when the path that led him there is examined more closely.

The biggest clue came from Atlanta. The Hawks had a $24.3 million team option for Kuminga and declined it in June. That decision immediately changed the market around a player who had once been viewed as a long-term piece in Golden State.

It also explains why the Minnesota contract looks so different from the salary attached to his previous season. Kuminga had been making $22.5 million, but Atlanta decided it would rather walk away from the chance to pay him $24.3 million.
Former NBA star Gilbert Arenas did not view the situation as a typical free-agent decision.

At 23 years old, the former No. 7 pick still had the age, athleticism and flashes of production that made him one of the league's most interesting young forwards.

articles.title: Mayer and Cameron split by security after clash at weigh-in
articles.summary: Mikaela Mayer and Chantelle Cameron had to be split by security as an amicable build-up erupted into a surprise war of words at Friday's fiery final weigh-in.
body: The two rivals locked foreheads in the middle of the stage before trading insults as a fired-up Cameron vowed to "smash her head in" ahead of Saturday's blockbuster super-welterweight world title fight in Birmingham.
American Mayer (22-2, 5 KOs), the WBA and WBC belt-holder, came in at 148lbs and three pounds lighter than her last fight against Mary Spencer back in October 2025.
WBO champion Cameron (22-1, 8 KOs) followed in at 147.6lbs for what will mark her second contest at super-welterweight after April's victory over Michaela Kotaskova.

It beckons as one of the most high-profile fights in women's boxing, Mayer having reigned as a three-weight world champion and two-weight world champion Cameron the only woman to beat Katie Taylor in the Irish icon's professional career.

articles.title: Trailblazer Taylor on 'strange' but 'amazing' England fielding coach role
articles.summary: Sarah Taylor says her landmark role as England men's fielding coach has been "strange" but "amazing" and that she is loving working with wicketkeeper Jamie Smith.
body: Former England women's player Taylor, regarded as one of the best wicketkeepers the game has seen, began her role with the senior men's side team this summer, following coaching stints with England Lions, Sussex and in The Hundred.
The 37-year-old is the first woman to coach an England men's side in a major sport.

Speaking to Sky Sports Cricket's Ian Ward prior to day two of the second Test against Pakistan at Lord's, Taylor said of her job: "It is a bit strange but what's brilliant about these guys is that they just call me coach.
"That's exactly what you want. I am entering their space so I have to respect their space. I have genuinely loved it, felt so welcome.
